chapter: Left out of the jazz books; Tatum, Handy and family
title: More recordings with Mildred Bailey and Fletcher Henderson; 'like the shadow'
summary: He lists Mildred Bailey dates, cannot recall his Henderson recordings, and says he is like a shadow though he spent fourteen years with Nat.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Well, some of those things that I did -- I did so many with Vic Dickenson, I'd just not name them. And Mildred Bailey. I did so many recordings with her, I'm just going back then. I'm not talking about now, I'm going back to those days. And here's some that I did with Mildred Bailey. I think Alec Wilder was the conductor. You know.
You did-- you said that you can't remember which things that you recorded with Fletcher Henderson.

I can't remember -- I think I did Stealing Apples or something. But I forget, it's been so long ago. You know, and -- but this I can't -- I was with Smack's band. That's a matter of record. You know. How can they not write about me? I mean, just for musical history, this is -- I don't understand it.
I'm like the shadow, you know. And as I say I was with -- even -- I left Tatum to join Nat. I was with Nat for 14 years.
